items.text: Children adopted a declaration at a children's climate consultation in Juba on 29 October, calling on the government and world leaders ahead of COP31 in Turkiye for climate-resilient schools, accessible early warning systems, emergency shelters and predictable funding for community-based adaptation. Save the Children South Sudan is finalising an assessment of climate-related loss and damage across several states, focused on flooding effects on children. The Ministry of Environment and Forestry says it is pursuing a US$25 million proposal with UNDP and plans a further US$15 million for small-scale farmers; the article stresses these are proposals, not secured or disbursed funds, and notes ministry work on nature-based solutions and recovery in flood-affected areas of Jonglei and Unity states.

The OCHA South Sudan Humanitarian Update for 16-30 October says the FEWS NET Science Team's 23 October assessment described June-September 2026 as the driest such season in the record beginning in 1981, with more than 80 per cent of the country in extreme or exceptional meteorological drought; satellite monitoring still recorded 33,018 km2 of inundation by mid-October, down from 41,111 km2 in August. Crisis (IPC Phase 3) is projected in 40 counties and Emergency (IPC Phase 4) in 32 counties from October 2026 to January 2027, and government estimates put more than 4 million people as affected by failed rains. Local authorities in Lafon County (Eastern Equatoria) reported hunger-related deaths after widespread crop failure; prolonged dry conditions in Nasir County (Upper Nile) forced families to move closer to water; and the Greater Pibor Administrative Area declared a drought emergency across eight counties (counties not named).

The OCHA South Sudan Humanitarian Update for 16-30 October says the cholera outbreak continues to decline but localized transmission persists: as of 21 October, 112,323 cumulative cases and 1,728 deaths across 55 counties (case fatality rate 1.5 per cent). Between 15 and 21 October, 40 new cases and no deaths were reported in Fangak (26), Renk (7), Rubkona (4) and Mayom (3); over 22 September-21 October the highest caseloads were in Renk (79), Fangak (59), Rubkona (39) and Mayom (31), and Mayom had the highest case fatality rate at 6.5 per cent. The earliest possible outbreak-over date cited is 18 November 2026, a conditional projection and not an official declaration.

items.scope: Jonglei, Unity and Upper Nile states
items.text: The UK has provided 2.1 million pounds (US$2.8 million) to FAO and WFP to expand anticipatory action in South Sudan; according to the joint FAO-WFP news release, the funding will support anticipatory flood interventions in Jonglei, Unity and Upper Nile states, including early-warning support, anticipatory cash assistance, livelihood protection and prepositioning of supplies, running until March 2027, as South Sudan braces for El Nino-induced drought and flood conditions.

The Lakes State government has declared a state of disaster after drought devastated crops; caretaker governor Riny Tueny Mabor urged households to stock food rather than wait for donors, and State Information Minister William Koji Kerjok appealed to donors and agencies for urgent help and warned the crisis could deteriorate into famine without immediate intervention.

The FEWS NET Global Weather Hazards Summary for 29 October-4 November 2026 says inundation in the Sudd wetlands of South Sudan persists, while large 90-day rainfall deficits caused abnormal dryness across South Sudan and neighbouring areas and drought-driven deterioration of vegetation was observed over South Sudan. It also forecasts abnormal heat in western South Sudan for the coming week, and notes that El Nino continues to strengthen.

Lakes State says it is working with authorities in Central and Western Equatoria to let pastoralists temporarily move livestock there in search of water and grazing land amid worsening dry conditions; the state government, which declared a state of disaster after prolonged dry spells, attributes the dry conditions to El Nino weather patterns.

UN Deputy Special Representative, Resident Coordinator ad interim and Humanitarian Coordinator Ramanathan Balakrishnan, at a high-level ministerial ad hoc committee meeting on durable solutions for displaced people in Bentiu, said persistent high water levels and a possible super El Nino could increase flood risks in the Bentiu area, and said what may have been viewed as a longer-term contingency has to be treated as an immediate preparedness priority; the article's lead says the UN warns Bentiu could face severe flooding sooner than anticipated. Kuyok Abol Kuyok, a caretaker minister speaking for the humanitarian affairs minister, cited recurrent flooding, limited financial resources and inadequate resilient infrastructure among the challenges and called for investment in drainage, raised roads and flood protection (county inferred from Bentiu).

The South Sudan Meteorological Service's forecast for 20 to 28 October covers areas including Lainya, Yei, Morobo and Kajo-Keji in Central Equatoria; it expects moderate rainfall of 50 to 100 mm in parts of several states, including Eastern Equatoria, and of the Pibor Administrative Area, and warns communities and road users in heavier-rainfall areas to remain alert to the possibility of waterlogging, localized flooding and road or bridge damage or disruption.

UK Ambassador Rebecca Fabrizi announced an extra 2.35 million pounds to reduce El Nino-linked risks in South Sudan; the article also cites a FEWS NET report that warns El Nino-related rainfall deficits could reduce the 2026 harvest and widen food gaps, and that identifies Jonglei and southern Upper Nile as areas where the combined effects of climate shocks and conflict could have particularly severe consequences.

Emmanuel Majok Brown, chairperson of the Mvolo Cooperative Union, says farmers in Mvolo County face widespread crop losses after too little rain in May and June, including a June dry spell that reportedly lasted one to one and a half months, and warns that famine could hit the area in the next few months; he says households have used up last year's food stocks and that limited maize arriving from parts of Mundri County may not meet local demand.

Lakes State caretaker governor Rin Tueny Mabor, speaking in Rumbek, warned of possible hunger, saying May and June rainfall was insufficient for cultivation and rains that began in October came too late for this year's farming season; he said northern parts of the state were facing serious water and pasture shortages that could force cattle keepers to move herds towards southern Lakes and neighbouring areas (county not stated for the shortages).

WFP's Matthew Hollingworth says the agency faces an $86 million funding gap now and a further $416 million gap over the next six months, and warns that more than one million vulnerable people could lose access to lifesaving food and nutrition assistance by October unless additional funding is secured; he says 7.8 million people struggle to find food each day as South Sudan faces conflict, displacement, economic hardship and climate shocks. At Canal Pigi in Jonglei he met families whose farmland remained submerged seven years after the original floods, while drought affects limited areas of cultivable land.
